title: Leading his own small groups and Decatur Street joints
summary: He led a four-piece at the Dandy Inn, a trio, and played with Johnny St. Cyr around Decatur Street.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I used to get a lot of weight myself, and I used to get a little line up, you know? Sure. I had a line up, a four-piece line up. I had myself, Albert Tablin on trumpet, Albert Giles on drums, and Clannis Gabriel on piano, four pieces. We used to play at the Dandy Inn. That was on Jefferson Davis.
I heard you out there. You did? 1938, about.
I know a little bit later in that. It was later in that.
Oh, he went out there a good while until he got ready to close down. Then after that, well, after that, there was trios was taking things over, you know? Yeah. Yeah. Had a lot of weight for trails.
I used to hear you out on Magazine Street one time with a trio too, a guitar.

Yeah, well, I got a three-piece lined up of my own. I had, I called it the three Ls. It was, I was playing piano then, Albert Giles playing drums, and I had Al, Al, playing ghetto. I guess that's the one I heard.
You worked with Johnny St. Sarah then later too, didn't you, for a while?

I worked around, well, I worked, yeah, I worked around, on Decatur Street, they had a lot of joints on Decatur Street, before Budapest Street got popped in. I played around there with a lot of three and four-piece bands. I played around there with Johnny St. Sarah too. Johnny St. Sarah played with me an old Lego band one time.
